name: DocILE
description: This paper introduces the DocILE benchmark with the largest dataset of business documents for the tasks of Key Information Localization and Extraction and Line Item Recognition. It contains 6.7k annotated business documents, 100k synthetically generated documents, and nearly~1M unlabeled documents for unsupervised pre-training. The dataset has been built with knowledge of domain- and task-specific aspects, resulting in the following key features: (i) annotations in 55 classes, which surpasses the granularity of previously published key information extraction datasets by a large margin; (ii) Line Item Recognition represents a highly practical information extraction task, where key information has to be assigned to items in a table; (iii) documents come from numerous layouts and the test set includes zero- and few-shot cases as well as layouts commonly seen in the training set. The benchmark comes with several baselines, including RoBERTa, LayoutLMv3 and DETR-based Table Transformer; applied to both tasks of the DocILE benchmark, with results shared in this paper, offering a quick starting point for future work. The dataset, baselines and supplementary material are available at https://github.com/rossumai/docile.
evaluation_method: F1 (entity-level/micro/macro F1; localization also evaluated with IoU/mAP-style metrics for regions)
general_score_metric: F1 (primary metric reported for extraction tasks)
typical_sota_score: ≈60–85% F1 (varies substantially by task, class granularity and layout subset)
reputation: Well-regarded in the document understanding community as a large, fine-grained business-document benchmark with published baselines (RoBERTa, LayoutLMv3, DETR variants).
notes: Contains 6.7k annotated documents plus large synthetic and unlabeled corpora for pretraining; test includes zero-/few-shot layouts. Moderate dataset size by modern standards, potential layout bias, and contamination risk if models were pretrained on overlapping corporate document sources.
